note: WHAT A DAY EARNS BEYOND ITS PAY. `Platform\Attendance\DaySettlement` has computed `overtimeMinutes` for every settled day since Phase 4, and NOTHING has ever read it. The attendance screen printed it in a column and no comp-off was ever credited, no overtime was ever paid, and no rule could have said otherwise because this decision point had no rules published against it. A figure computed on every page load and consumed by nobody is not a feature; it is a number that makes a screen look complete. These rules are evaluated at `attendance.day.earn`, whose conflict policy is ALL_MATCH — a single day can earn overtime AND a comp-off, and a decision point that returns only the winner would hand somebody one of the two.
why_a_separate_file: One file per decision point, as with leave-rules.json. attendance.day.classify answers 'what kind of day was this' and takes the highest-priority answer; this one answers 'what did it earn' and takes every answer. Sharing a file would put two different conflict policies under one heading and invite somebody to move a rule between them.

comp_off.note: The leave type a comp-off is credited to. Named here rather than in code, and the credit is REFUSED if config/leave-policy.json does not declare it — crediting days to a type nobody has declared writes a balance no screen shows and no payroll spends.

rules.name: A full day worked on a weekly off earns a comp-off
rules.description: Somebody who works a full shift on their weekly off has given up a day and is owed one. Credited as a day in the leave ledger rather than paid, because that is what the great majority of Indian employers do and because a ledger entry can be argued with, reversed and encashed — where an extra line on one month's payslip cannot.

then.reason: Full shift worked on a weekly off

rules.name: A full day worked on a declared holiday earns a comp-off
rules.description: The same for a holiday. Separate from the weekly-off rule rather than merged with an OR, because they are two policies that customers routinely set differently — plenty of employers pay for a holiday and give time back for a weekly off — and one rule doing both cannot be changed independently.

then.reason: Full shift worked on a declared holiday

rules.name: Overtime beyond the shift, on a working day
rules.description: Minutes worked past the shift on an ordinary working day are recorded as overtime. RECORDED, not paid: nothing in this build computes an overtime rate, and a rule that emitted an amount would be inventing one. The entry is what a payroll administrator sees and decides about, and the day a multiplier is declared it is this same rule that feeds it.
rules.when: attendance.ot_minutes > 0m AND NOT day.is_weekly_off AND NOT day.is_holiday
